source.title: Low-Pass Filtering SGD for Recovering Flat Optima in the Deep Learning Optimization Landscape
source.authors: Devansh Bisla; Jing Wang; A. Choromańska

page_placements.theme: Loss curvature and parameter displacement track some interpolation peaks

record.tranche_reason: The study varies neural-network width and measures validation error to examine model-wise double descent, using the same basic capacity-sweep and error-curve approach as the claim.
record.gate_note: The width-sweep results in Supplementary Section 11.4 and Figure 7 bear on V1. Other epoch-versus-error plots compare training optimizers and do not test epoch-wise double descent. The experiments varying label-noise or data-noise levels do not vary the amount of training data, so they do not test V3. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: Supplement 11.4 reruns the Nakkiran et al. width sweep: ResNet18 with widths [k,2k,4k,8k], CIFAR-10, 20% label noise, Adam, 4000 epochs. It plots validation error against width (Figure 7), which bears directly on V1. The sweep is a side experiment; its purpose is to test whether sharpness measures track double descent. The double-descent shape of the validation error is only implied by the authors' wording and the figure. No error values are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it overstates the double-descent part, which is a supplementary side result. The paper's main conclusions are about sharpness. The LPF sharpness measure correlates best with generalization and is robust to data and label noise. LPF-SGD outperforms SGD, SAM and other flatness-seeking optimizers. On double descent, the authors say it is 'sometimes' observed as capacity grows. In their ResNet18 width sweep, most flatness measures track it, LPF most closely.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies ResNet18 width and measures validation error, but the reported setting uses CIFAR-10 with 20% label noise, Adam, and 4000 training epochs, and emphasizes comparison of sharpness measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The double-descent width sweep is conducted with 20% label noise, Adam, a batch size of 128, a constant learning rate of 1e−4, and 4000 epochs; no alternative conditions for this sweep are reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the noisy-label width sweep, the Kendall correlation between each sharpness measure and validation error is: LPF 0.851 (highest), ||H||F 0.823, FRN 0.810, Trace(H) 0.794, λmax 0.778, ε-sharpness 0.774, Shannon 0.617, PAC-Bayes 0.440, deff 0.149, μLE -0.141.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-landscape sharpness measures (especially LPF and Hessian-norm measures) track the model-wise double-descent curve in validation error; Hessian effective dimensionality and local-entropy gradient do not.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, 2022
record.problems: The double-descent curve is presented as a figure without numeric error values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The reported measure is validation error, and the width-sweep result is limited to one architecture, dataset, and noisy-label setting.

untested.parts: Other architectures, datasets and noise levels. No clean-label (0% noise) sweep. Peak location relative to the interpolation threshold is not reported.
Not tested. Epoch-vs-error plots compare optimizers on standard training, not epoch-wise double descent.
Not tested. Training-set size is never varied.
Not tested. Label noise is fixed at 20% for the width sweep, and regularization is not varied in it.
Not tested. deff is correlated with error, but error is not replotted against effective parameters.

record.verdict_notes: The study is a sharpness/optimizer paper; the width sweep appears only in Supplement 11.4. Table 2/Table 10 vary width only over {32,48,64} on clean labels and report generalization gap, not a capacity sweep through interpolation, so they do not bear on V1. No seeds or uncertainty are reported for the width sweep. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The width sweep is one ResNet18 setup on CIFAR-10 with 20% label noise; other architectures, datasets, and settings are not tested for this version.
